Wendelle Stevens Cheats His Authors Correction




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2009 > Oct > Oct 16

                                      Wendelle Stevens Cheats His Authors Correction
  From: Richard Heiden <rwheidenu.nul>
  Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2009 12:55:08 -0700 (PDT)
  Archived: Fri, 16 Oct 2009 10:22:00 -0400
  Subject: Wendelle Stevens Cheats His Authors Correction

  On March 18, postedhere was my translation of Zitha Rodriguez's
  article, Wendelle Stevens Cheats His Authors.
  James Moseley declined to print anything on Wendelle Stevens's
  literary piracy in his "Saucer Smear" newsletter, writing (April
  3), "Col. Stevens is so _far_out_ of mainstream ufoology [sic]
  that I don't consider him worth exposing. Years ago, =E2=80=98Smear'
  ran an _exclusive_ when he was sent to prison for fooling around
  with young girls."
  Jim also wrote that he did not believe the 1,400,000-copy sales
  figure for Zitha's book ("IMPOSSIBLE!" he annotated when he
  returned the article). I have to say that it seemed high to me
  too, but figured that in another country (like Turkey, which has
  a pirated edition of the book) the public might have a great
  interest in the subject of UFOs, plus books might be really
  cheap there. As it turns out, I should indeed have questioned
  Zitha about it. In response to my belated request for her
  source, she sent me scanned copies of two print-outs from
  Amazon.com, of the page offering the book for sale. What Zitha
  took as the number of copies sold, was really "Sales rank,"
  which is something quite different.
  I am including below a slightly edited version of the complete
  article. Not just to remove the mistaken sales figures for the
  book (as explained above). I have also edited certain characters
  that came through goofy when the article was originally
  circulated--I have now removed the Spanish accents and replaced
  with regular English letters the special Turkish letters ("s"
  with a cedilla in "Akasa"; undotted "i"; plus other characters
  on the Turkish Web site at the end, which the previous posting
  had omitted).
  My apologies for not catching this error before. Of course, it
  does not make it OK for Wendelle to get books reprinted behind
  the authors' backs=E2=80=94it just means that the financial
  ramifications aren't nearly as great as Zitha might have
  thought.
  Richard Heiden
  Milwaukee
  Cc:
  Zitha Rodriguez Montiel <zitharm.nul>
  ---
  The Story Of A Book That Was Lost In A Sea Of Confusion, Lies,
  And Plagiarism
  By Zitha Rodriguez Montiel
  Translated by Richard W. Heiden
  In 1979, the author interviewed Professor R.N. Hernandez,
  professor with the National Autonomous University of Mexico
  (Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico, or UNAM).
  The professor claimed to this author that he had had a close
  contact with an extraterrestrial woman. That was how the idea of


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m16-007.shtml[11/12/2011 23:11:18]
Wendelle Stevens Cheats His Authors Correction

  writing a book about his history was born. It was written by the
  author of this article.
  The book's original Spanish title is "Profecias de una Mujer
  Extraterrestre" ("Prophecies of an Extraterrestrial Woman") and,
  as the name indicates, this lady gave the professor many
  predictions about our future, especially climactic changes that
  would be produced in our days.
  The book was recorded in Mexico's Instituto Nacional de Derechos
  de Autor (National Copyright Institute), in the year 1985.
  In 1988, the author got in touch with Wendelle C. Stevens,
  publisher and editor of UFO Photo Archives, and proposed to him
  that he publish the book. Wendelle, who at that time lived in
  Florence, Ariz., accepted the book for publication. He
  translated it to English and changed the title to:
  "UFO CONTACT FROM ANDROMEDA"
  It was copyrighted and given the International Standard Book
  Number (ISBN), 0-934269-12-2.
  When it was published, the author received as payment only forty
  copies from Wendelle.
  At the same time, Wendelle promised Zitha Rodriguez that he
  would forward to her any profits from the book, which never
  happened.
  As time passed, and over a period of at least ten years, the
  author received over two thousand letters from people who
  assured her they had bought the book and were interested in the
  story of Professor Hernandez.
  Between the years 1989 and 1993, whenever the author inquired
  about the book, Wendelle C. Stevens would tell her that very few
  copies had been sold, and that the book was not going to be
  reprinted.
  In 1994, when the author attended the UFO Congress in Mesquite,
  Nevada, she saw that the book was available for sale.
  At that same Congress, Wendelle told the author that he had very
  few copies of the book left, and that he would not print any
  more because nobody was interested in it. Also present when he
  said this was Patricia Olopa (also of Mexico), who heard
  everything.
  Then the author asked Wendelle to not print it any more because
  she had plans to publish it in Mexico. Wendelle promised that he
  wouldn't. Nevertheless, the next year, in 1995, Wendelle
  authorized Akasa Yayinlari (Akasa Publishing) to publish the
  book in Turkish, and it was distributed in that country. See:
  http://tinyurl.com/yfrdunr
  The author learned of this from the Internet only in 2003,
  through a friend, because Wendelle never notified her.
  The translator who rendered the work from English to Turkish
  must have had quite a challenge, because of the very poor
  quality of the translation from Spanish. Wendelle received the
  manuscript when he was incarcerated in Arizona, and the author
  seems to recall that he said at the time that he received
  assistance from a fellow convict who spoke both English and
  Spanish. Though in the book itself that he published, Wendelle
  took full credit for the translation.*
  The author wrote to Akasa Publishing at an address obtained from
  a friend in Ankara, but the publisher never responded to
  repeated e-mails.
  But the betrayal and lies on Wendelle's part did not stop there.
  In 2004, Wendelle authorized Robert ("Bob") Shapiro, of Light
  Technology Publishing to not only publish the above-mentioned
  book, but also to add the story of a medium, who claimed to have
  mental contact with Prof. Hernandez. This was an offense on the
  work itself, as it deformed the original idea, and the author
  was not notified of this.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m16-007.shtml[11/12/2011 23:11:18]
Wendelle Stevens Cheats His Authors Correction


  This book was titled:
  "Ultimate UFO Series: Andromeda/Channeled Commentary
  by Andromedans & Zoosh Through Robert Shapiro"
  Below that (on both the cover and the title page) it says:
  "Includes the text of UFO Contact From Andromeda
  Extraterrestrial Prophecy
  (c) UFO Books: Rodriguez Hernandez Stevens"
  And below that, the logo and name of Light Technology
  Publishing.
  The copyright page adds the ISBN, 1-891824-35-X.
  At the top of the copyright page it says that pages 167-459 were
  taken from the above-mentioned book. Though it identifies the
  book only by date and publisher, it is an obvious reference to
  "UFO Contact from Andromeda."
  When the author again got in touch with Wendelle, to express her
  disapproval concerning this development, Wendelle advised her to
  speak with Bob. Bob never responded to the Internet messages
  that the author sent him. Thus time passed.
  Realizing that Wendelle did not answer the author's mail
  anymore, Zitha Rodriguez asked a U.S.-Mexican attorney to speak
  with Wendelle about it, but the latter always denied having
  authorized Akasa Publishing and Light Technology Publishing to
  publish the book.
  Until now, neither Wendelle, nor Akasa, nor Bob Shapiro, have
  responded to the author's entreaties. Perhaps they are waiting
  for her to tire of wailing in the desert.
  The author desires these facts to be known so that the guilty
  parties do not remain unpunished, and that other authors do not
  suffer the same thing. But it would be interesting to know if
  there have already been other victims.
  With these events, the author feels betrayed, attacked, and ill-
  served in her interests by Wendelle C. Stevens, because she
  fully confided, in good faith, in the word of the publisher of
  UFO Photo Archives.
  Zitha Rodriguez Montiel
  Mexico City
  zitharm2003.nul
  *I remember Wendelle's talk at the UFO congress that Zitha
  organized in Mexico City in August of 1995. Wendelle acted as
  his own translator, speaking in both English and fractured
  Spanish. It was (I must say) a brave effort, but with rather
  pathetic results. Even though he and Randolph Winters were
  speaking about the Billy Meier case of Switzerland, Wendelle's
  translation kept giving the name of the country as "Suizlandia"
  rather than "Suiza," which is the correct word in Spanish.--
  Trans.
  Postscript by translator:
  Since this article was originally written in 2007, I have
  learned of two more books that Wendelle has arranged to get
  reprinted without the knowledge of the author. In one case, the
  author got in touch with the republisher after the fact to
  negotiate royalties. He reports that "I would like to keep my
  arrangement private. I do not have anything against [the
  publisher]. He treated me very well."
  In the other case, Wendelle arranged for the re-publication not
  too long after the author asked him about getting the text of
  the book on a disc, with a view toward facilitating a reprint.
  At that time "he said there was not much interest in the book."

  Fellow Listerions,
  We are coming up to a year since charges were filed against Bill
  Knell for copyright infringement violations (a federal felony
  offense); the authorities, including local Lebanon, Indiana
  (where Knell resides) police as well as multiple FBI agents for
  months now, have had "physical evidence in hand," documentive
  evidence," and "electronic evidence (his web-site)" and "written
  formal complaints" from some of the victims, yet Knell has been
  allowed to continue to operate; in fact, he is at an all time
  high, and has even branched out to "Amazon."
  His modus operandi is to "pirate" DVDs, either professionally
  produced documentaries e.g., Out of The Blue, or video taped
  lectures from various symposia in which case the promoters
  usually hold copyright and then to sell them via the internet,
  either on his web-site and or other sites like Amazon. Knell's
  criminal activities have gone on for decades e.g., before DVDs
  it was VHS tapes; he has been successfully sued by some of
  victims, only to relocate and start again; he is a career
  criminal.
  Early on when he felt the heat he removed some of the more
  obvious pirated DVDs, e.g., Out of The Blue, only to re-list
  them when he felt more comfortable (as he does now);
  additionally, when he has been confronted from victims
  (individually) who are ignorant to his conman persona, he will
  happily remove the example and claim his own ignorance--this is
  his long time methodology which he has down to a science. When
  he feels the coast is clear, he re-lists the the pirated
  material and goes about this business.
  It's a mystery why the the authorities seem to be dragging their
  feet; however, and in my opinion it at least in part is because
  they're only hearing one voice and that has been from victim,
  "Scott Ramsey." He has been carrying the ball for "all of the
  victims" and it's my thinking they (the authorities) are not
  perceiving the gravity of this matter.
  It's important to point out this scenario exists in part because
  the lead detective i.e., Maurice Hobson asked for patience, and
  for victims to file a complaint locally with their respective
  police departments and have those complaints forwarded to him,
  which was done by a "few"proactive victims, e.g., Don Ledger,
  Linda Howe et al (thank you); in essence just let him do his
  job. Consequently, Scott stepped up to the plate, and basically
  became the "go-between" for some of the proactive victims and
  the authorities.
  Months ago out of frustration (for nothing happening), I
  contacted a law enforcement colleague of mine who is also a UFO
  enthusiast and asked his advise; he said we were wasting our
  energy at the wrong level, as this is a "federal crime." Acting
  on his advise, Scott then filed a criminal complaint with the
  FBI; at this time we felt finally, something would be done about
  this criminal; unfortunately, this has not been the case; it
  appears that there are just more people "dragging their feet."
  Perhaps if the victims were not authors of "UFO" minutiae a more

                                                Re: Magnetic Electricity Discovered
  From: Martin Shough <parcellular.nul>
  Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2009 20:24:15 +0100
  Archived: Sat, 17 Oct 2009 08:29:00 -0400
  Subject: Re: Magnetic Electricity Discovered

  >From: Greg Boone <Evolbaby.nul>
  >To: post.nul
  >Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2009 00:17:42 EDT
  >Subject: Magnetic Electricity Discovered
  >Soooo, here we are again having to rewrite the science and
  >history books.
  I'm afraid that here we are again misunderstanding basic science
  and basic history.
  >http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/technology/8307804.stm
  >What was postulated 100 years ago is now a fact. I'm quite sure
  >there are scores of volumes of skeptical texts that swore up and
  >down this new discovery was an impossibility because scientists
  >knew_everything already.
  >I'm beginning to think some scientists are paid to say something
  >isn't or can't or won't just so they'll get a jump on the
  >competition and snag the patents and military contracts.

  The impression given here is that establishment physics has
  spent 100 years resisting evidence for magnetic monopoles until
  some heroic maverick finally proves that Big Science was wrong.
  This is a complete travesty and an inversion of the facts.
  Firstly, magnetic monopoles have been predicted and expected by
  physicists ever since Dirac on the strength of basic symmetry
  principles that are the foundation of mainstream theory. The
  puzzle has always been: Why aren't there any? Or if there are
  any, where are they? Their discovery now would not puncture any
  claims of "impossibility" - it would fully justify physicists'
  belief in their theoretical inevitability.
  But secondly, they have not in fact been found. The phenomena
  referred to are not true natural magnetic monopoles in the sense
  required - i.e., isolated quanta of magnetic charge having N or
  S polarity analogous to the isolated quanta of electric charge
  having - or + polarity that we call electrons or positrons. They
  are instead "quasi-particles", made of strings of magnetic
  charges that can be encouraged to behave _like_ magnetic
  monopoles inside a very specialised material. Interesting, but
  not the real McCoy.
  An analogy in electronics would be the way in which a "hole" in
  a matrix of negative charges can behave like an isolated
  positive charge which moves about and can be manipulated like a
  particle. But this quasi-particle of charge would not satisfy
  the need for a positive electric charge (anti-electron) which is
  implied by phsyical theory. That true positive charge quantum is
  the positron. The magnetic analogues of separable electron-
  positron pairs have yet to be found - and may not exist (which
  would clearly be a very important discovery).

  Martin Shough

  Years ago we had a con man systematically fleecing the rare book
  trade all over the world via mail order, offering dealers rare
  books for a couple of hundred dollars, cashing the checks, and
  not sending the books (which he didn't possess anyway). The sums
  were not sufficient for any individual dealer to put much effort
  into pursuing, and too small for any local law enforcement to be
  interested. It was only once this fellow forged his granny's
  signature and sold almost $100,000 of her stock and bonds, that
  the FBI became interested. We were told at the time that
  $100,000 in losses was the minimum that would get their
  attention. I suspect that these days budgetary considerations
  would put an even higher floor for required damages.
  However, given the way Knell is operating, you have a few more
  options available. Are civil rather than criminal suits
  possible? Have the parties who are hurt by his activities filed
  complaints with his ISP, his Mastercard and Visa facilitators,
  the advertising company that supplies the banner ads on his
  website, Amazon itself? I see that there are really very few
  reviews of any sort for his Amazon products, and those are
  countered by the gushing 5 star reviews by "C. Knell "Montauk
  Fan" (presumably Catherine Knell). Note that bogus negative
  reviews are just as possible as bogus positive reviews -- while
  Amazon will examine them if complaints are made, they will want
  to see evidence to support the complaints.
  This online FAQ
  http://tinyurl.com/yjwtvwo

  sufficient number of the pirated DVDs were sold to make
  prosecution worthwhile. I don't see that Amazon would (or
  should) release that information without a lot of legal
  pressure. Not to mention the giggle factor inherent in UFO
  lawsuits.

http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m17-008.shtml[11/12/2011 23:11:24]
Re: Victims Of Bill Knell

  3.3) Is copyright infringement a crime, or a civil matter?
  It's always at least a civil matter (a tort). 17 U.S.C. 501(b)
  details the mechanisms by which an owner of a copyright may file
  a civil suit, and 28 U.S.C. 1338 expressly refers to civil
  actions arising under the copyright act.
  However, under certain circumstances, it may also be a federal
  crime. A copyright infringement is subject to criminal
  prosecution if infringement is willful and for purposes of
  commercial advantage or private financial gain. 17 U.S.C.
  506(a). If the offense consists of the reproduction or
  distribution, during any 180-day period, of 10 or more copies
  having a retail value of more than $2,500, the offense is a
  felony; otherwise, the offense is a misdemeanor. 18 U.S.C.
  2319."

  Carol Maltby

                                                      Shag Harbour And Tourism
  From: Don Ledger <dledger.nul>
  Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2009 11:08:35 -0300
  Archived: Sat, 17 Oct 2009 10:35:00 -0400
  Subject: Shag Harbour And Tourism

  Source: The Chronicle Herald - Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada
  http://thechronicleherald.ca/Letters/1147711.html
  Thu. Oct 15 2009
  A Shot In The Arm For Local Tourism
  by Don Ledger
  Regarding "Shag Harbour's 'UFO incident' sets scene for Sounding
  Line" by Stephen Patrick Clare in the Books section (Oct. 11):
  I would like to congratulate Anne DeGrace on the publication of
  her novel. As one of the two authors of Dark Object, the book
  that alerted the world to this event, as well as numerous
  documentaries and lectures, I would like to share a few
  observations.
  The Shag Harbour incident is now one of the most well-known
  unidentified flying object events in UFO history.
  It is often mistakenly referred to as Canada's Roswell - a
  misnomer which implies that, like the Roswell incident, there is
  no documentary evidence.
  In fact, the actual event in Shag Harbour is heavily documented.
  The Chronicle Herald's stories, the CBC's film footage of the
  search, and government documents revealed the ongoing operation
  in Shag Harbour.
  They reveal the involvement of Maritime Command, the RCAF's Air
  Desk in Ottawa, the RCMP and the Rescue Co-ordination Centre
  (RCC) in Halifax.
  It is now clear that an object "landed" - not crashed - on the
  waters off Shag Harbour.
  A dozen local residents reported an airplane crashing in Shag
  Harbour and never mentioned a UFO. Other residents and three
  RCMP officers watched a drifting light on the water, and made
  plans to go out and rescue or assist the survivors. Young
  fishermen reported knots in their stomachs at the prospect of
  seeing the mutilated bodies of victims.
  The initial event unfolds like the crashing of an airplane.
  Having written another book, Swissair Down, about the crash of
  Flight 111, it is my opinion the RCC, the RCMP and the local
  fishermen reacted in the same manner in both cases.
  In the days that followed, it was military documents that
  labelled the object a UFO.
  Anne DeGrace and I discussed this incident in Shag Harbour in
  October of 2007. Her success in getting the book published, and
  the possibility of a movie, also helps promote the area.
  This year, some 1,100 people from across North America and from


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m17-009.shtml[11/12/2011 23:11:24]
Shag Harbour And Tourism

  Europe visited the temporary museum in Shag Harbour.
  Recently, a cruise ship line docking in Shelburne asked
  representatives from the museum to be available to the
  passengers when its vessel docks there on Oct. 25.
  Hopefully, Anne DeGrace's book will further invigorate tourism
  interest in the area, which could use another industry to
  buttress a declining fishery.

  Don Ledger is co-author of Dark Object and author of Swissair
  Down and Maritime UFO Files. He lives in Molega Lake.

  I don't want technical data out on the table to be used by our
  enemies. However, if there was disclosure of how many planes
  have been destroyed while chasing UFOs, of how many UFO crashes
  there have been and when and where, it would certainly lift the
  laughter curtain, would encourage other excellent witnesses to
  come forth, force the media to do some in depth investigation,
  get the United Nations involved much more.
  It would force religious leaders to examine their views on who
  we are, might force people on the planet to get together and
  reduce the amount of tribal warfare.
  It might also let us know if there are trade relations with
  aliens and who is selling what to whom. It might shut up a lot
  of nasty noisy negativists as well.
  I am certainly not expecting government disclosure soon. Don't
  forget that the best radar and satellite instrumentation for
  monitoring UFOs is under Government control.

  Stan Friedman

  understand how the social dynamics work.

  foreseeable future (short, of course, of - cliche alert - the
  White House landing or whatever), this discussion is about as
  meaningful as the proverbial debate about the size of the
  angelic dance party on a pin's head.

                                           Nobel Prizewinner & The Talking Racoon
  From: Dave Haith <visions1.nul>
  Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2009 00:35:25 +0100
  Archived: Tue, 20 Oct 2009 12:36:28 -0400
  Subject: Nobel Prizewinner & The Talking Racoon

  On Coast to Coast the other night I was listening to George
  Knapp interviewing Bill Chalker about his Hair of the Alien
  case.
  In passing, he mentioned a Nobel prizewinner for his work with
  DNA, who also may be an abductee.
  I had never heard of this before and Googled to discover he must
  have been referring to Kary Mullis who in 1993 won the Nobel
  prize for chemistry and his development of the Polymerase Chain
  Reaction in DNA analysis.
  I gather this enables scientists to identify a fragment of DNA
  genetic code and reproduce it in large measure.
  Some links here that are relevant:
  http://www.burlingtonnews.net/redhairedmummiesalienhybrids.html
  http://www.cufos.org/IUR_spring99_addendum.html
  http://www.dailygrail.com/news/kary-mullis-dna-lsd-and-alien-abductions
  [And in The UFO UpDates Archive going back to 1999:
    http://tinyurl.com/yfemgd7
    --ebk]
  The story goes that during a drive to his California cabin
  Mullis conceived his DNA discovery.
  At this same cabin a couple of years later he met a talking
  racoon in nearby woods, experienced six hours of missing time
  and found himself wandering along a local road.
  What I find really weird is that if Mullis hadn't invented the
  DNA analysis system Bill Chalker couldn't have used it to prove
  his hair of the alien case.
  Did aliens feed Mullis the DNA trick I wonder, so that it could
  be used later to confirm aliens really exist?
  Probably this is far too simplistic but I am fascinated to hear
  what other Listers make of this case.
  I gather that Mullis himself thinks the David Jacobs scenario of
  alien hybrids is unlikely because any culture conquering space
  time would have solved problems of biochemistry.
  He prefers to believe his experience may have been multi-
  dimensional where "anything can god-damn happen".

  Dave Haith

No-Witness UFO Photos




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2009 > Oct > Oct 22

                                                         No-Witness UFO Photos
  From: Jim Deardorff <deardorj.nul>
  Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2009 18:40:39 -0700
  Archived: Thu, 22 Oct 2009 09:09:00 -0400
  Subject: No-Witness UFO Photos

  This seems to be a relatively new, burgeoning phenomenon - UFO
  images noticed after the fact on cell phones, photographs and
  videos. Prior to two or three years ago, I would estimate, it
  was much less common than today. It is as if the UFO aliens
  recognize that "a photo alone does not a UFO make," so that they
  understand they can "get away" with increased grass-roots
  exposure in this manner without risking that science or ufology
  would latch onto it and thereby bring about a premature end to
  the coverup. The phenomenon often involves just one photo out of
  a rapid sequence of shots containing the UFO, or only one or a
  few frames of a video.
  It would be interesting if anyone on the list has kept track of
  this phenomenon, to be able to graph the rate of increase of
  such exposures over the past 10 or 20 years.
  Until this phenomenon becomes well known, it seems to me that it
  is less subject to hoaxing and mistaken identification than
  photos with anonymous witnesses. If my impression is correct,
  the taker of a non-witnessed UFO is less likely to insist on
  staying anonymous, and the UFO images involved seem to be of
  slightly better quality - less blurry or less distant, a higher
  percentage of daytime cases, etc. - than with photographed UFOs
  that are witnessed at the time.
  Of course, a photo of an alleged non-witnessed UFO is quite
  worthless if the photographer is unknown or cannot be reached
  for questioning.

  Jim Deardorff

  Hi Ed, Everyone,
  When one looks into modern accounts of alien abductions and past
  encounters with beings that came down from or who reside in the
  heavens, one should not overlook the significance of some very
  interesting and important observations that are common to nearly
  all these accounts.
  One of the most obvious of these observations is that these
  beings look very much like us. Another is that these beings can
  interbreed with humans. Yet another is that these beings know a
  lot about us and our history and seem to be concerned about our
  development and our future.
  Although we haven't yet (officially) discovered any intelligent
  life, including microbial life, beyond planet Earth, evolution
  trained biologists believe that once the spark of life catches
  on other worlds, the fire of evolution, over billions of years
  will produce a diversity of life forms similar to what we find
  on Earth.
  Since the conditions suitable for life on these other worlds may
  not be the same as Earth's and because evolutionary changes are
  the result of largely random events, the intelligent beings of
  these other worlds would not look like us at all.
  The fact that the visitors from above do closely resemble us
  physically, this taken together with reports of alien/human
  offspring (eg. Biblical accounts of angels having sexual
  encounters with humans; mythological accounts of Gods breeding
  with humans; modern accounts of alien/human offspring, etc.),
  all this is possible only if aliens and us are members of the
  same species.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m23-001.shtml[11/12/2011 23:11:44]
Re: Human & Alien Origins?


  These often overlooked facts strongly suggest that these beings
  are not extraterrestrials but "ultraterrestrials" (to borrow an
  expression from John Keel for the lack of a better term) whose
  home is also Earth and are very much a part of our own reality.
  If this deduction is correct, then they are not an impossible
  chance evolutionary match to us humans, they must have the same
  origins and even share a common Creator/God.

  Nick Balaskas

  side as is the Sky Cat Series in the UK. The SkyCat series are
  60% helium buoyant and are in developement.
  The L/M model is 80% bouyant[helium]and relies on 4-5 thrusters
  to move it fast enough to creat enough lift over its body to
  keep it airborne. These are designed to stay aloft for about
  three weeks with a payload of sensors and provide the US DoD
  with 'unblinking' surveillance while avoiding the threat of
  roadside bombs. They can loiter off well away from the action.
  >Third, I didn't say Raytheon made them, I merely said was linked
  >too. I can't remember the exact details, as the research from
  >the time is currently "archived" due to space restraints.
  In any event the closest Raytheon gets to an aircraft other than
  instrumentation is missile systems and air to air and air to
  ground missiles.
  >And finally, All three cases that I was involved in researching, had
  >near identical shape & lights, which, as I started my missive with
  >"reminds me of" <g>
  That should tell you something. Have you come to grips with why
  'stealth' aircraft would be flying around making nuisences of
  themselves, flashing any number of lights and drawing attention
  to themselves negating their stealth classification?
  Researchers often drag out the secret developement of the F117-A
  and how long that was kept secret. There is a good reason for
  that; they weren't flying it over Los Angeles or New York
  flashing a bunch of lights. They did their experimentations in
  secret at Groom Lake in Lincoln, Nevada, well away from
  civilians and highways. Same with the B2-B.
  I have spent many years researching the major powers aviation
  capabilities mainly to counter the convienient cope-out theory
  that many of these UFO sightings can be accounted for by
  'secret' military aircraft. Frankly if you know anything about
  aviation, it is a poorly devised explanation with little to
  support it and has been used since day one as an explanation for
  UFO reports; but in 99% of the cases [even the CIA tried this
  one] it never works out.

                                                          Useful Firefox Add-Ons
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <post.nul>
  Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2009 07:50:00 -0400
  Archived: Fri, 23 Oct 2009 07:50:00 -0400
  Subject: Useful Firefox Add-Ons



  Subscribers/Readers may find these Firefox Add-Ons useful:

  TinyUrl Creator 1.0.5
  https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/126
  TinyUrl lets you shrink any long URL in your address bar or link
  on the page to something you can easily email or Twitter with a
  single click.
  NEW: Now any link on a page that has a tinyurl.com address will
  contain a tooltip to tell you what the full URL for it is. Just
  hover your mouse over the link for a moment and you'll see the
  full URL appear as a tooltip.
  The TinyUrl Creator is accessible in the Tools menu and in the
  right-click context menu. You can even add it to your toolbars
  as an icon (View > Toolbars > Customize).
  ---
  AutoCopy 1.0
  https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/383
  Select text and it's automatically copied to the clipboard. Like
  Linux or mIRC.
  ---
  Domain Details 2.5
  https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/2166
  View the current site's server software and headers, IP address,
  location flag, and have quick links to Whois and other domain
  information. When a page fails to load, links are shown to check
  cache and server status.
  ---
  Tab Kit 0.5.8
  https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/5447
  Tab Kit makes tabs more efficient for power users, allowing a
  wide variety of tweaks, all of which are optional, notably:
  - Group tabs, by domain or opener (parent) tab, manually or automatically
  - Vertical tab tree (with splitter), like Tree Style Tab
  - Multi-row tabs
  - Sort tabs, by address, last loaded, last viewed, order of creation, origin or title
  - Control new tab position and close order
  - Easily duplicate tabs and groups and copy/move them between windows by dragging
  - Scrollwheel tab switch
  - 'Mouse rocker' to go back/forward in history


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m23-004.shtml[11/12/2011 23:11:46]
Useful Firefox Add-Ons

  - Highlight unread tabs (and emphasise current tab)
  - Scrollbar instead of scroll arrows in over-long Bookmarks and All Tabs popups
  - Open Selected Links feature
  - Switch tabs on hover
  - Options for urls, searches and/or bookmarks to open in new tabs by default
  ---
  gTranslate 0.5.1
  https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/918
  With gTranslate you can translate any text in a webpage just by
  selecting and right-clicking over it. The extension uses the
  Google translation services to translate the text.
  Features:
  * Translates from/to the following languages:
  - English
  - Arabic
  - Bulgarian
  - Chinese
  - Chinese (Simplified)
  - Chinese (Traditional)
  - Croatian
  - Czech
  - Danish
  - Dutch
  - Finnish
  - French
  - German
  - Greek
  - Hindi
  - Italian
  - Japanese
  - Korean
  - Norwegian
  - Polish
  - Portuguese
  - Romanian
  - Russian
  - Spanish
  - Swedish
  * Option to automatically identify the language of the original
    text.
  * Option to detect the "lang" attribute of the of the selected
    text (or the whole page).
  * Option to set the destination language to the browser locale.
  * Replace texts from input and textareas form fields.
  * Image title or alt attributes can be translated too.

Mac Tonnies Passes




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2009 > Oct > Oct 23

                                                             Mac Tonnies Passes

  From: Paul Kimball <robieshark.nul>
  To: UFO UpDates - Toronto <post.nul>
  Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2009 09:12:37 -0300
  Subject: Mac Tonnies Pases

  I have received word from Nick Redfern that my dear friend, Mac
  Tonnies, has passed away.
  There is so much I could say. There is so much I will say in the
  days to come. But for the moment, I'll share this memory:
  The last time Mac was in Halifax, shooting some interview
  segments for a documentary produced by another company here, he
  and I went out one night for a short drive that turned into a
  three hour marathon drive to nowhere, as we listened to the
  Smiths and talked about life, and the universe, and UFOs, and
  all the others things that you talk about with best friends.
  About thirty kilometres outside of Halifax, I noticed that the
  light on the gas gauge had gone on, meaning I was running low.
  Out in the rural area where we were, at that time of night,
  there were no service stations open. I told Mac I thought we had
  enough to get back to town, but then I added, mischievously,
  that I wasn't sure, and we might have to hoof it, in November.
  He just looked at me, said "figures that the first time I ever
  'ran out of gas' with someone it would be with you on a dark,
  lonely road in Nova Scotia." We both had a good laugh!
  In the days and weeks to come, those are the good memories that
  I will cherish, and share here.
  One more memory - when I ran the New Frontiers Symposium here in
  Halifax back in 2006, Mac was one of the guys on the bill, along
  with Nick, Greg Bishop, Stan Friedman, Will Wise and space
  historian Robert Zimmerman (and myself). Mac spoke on
  posthumanism, and gave one of the most engaging, and thought-
  provoking, talks you will ever hear, for 1 1/2 hours - with not
  a single note in front of him. That's how good he was.
  Mac's light, which burned brightly, but for far too short a
  time, will never go out. He will be missed more than he could
  have known.

  Paul Kimball

  Odd unintentionally photographed objects go back more than
  twenty years.
  There are some that go back as far as the 1930's and perhaps
  earlier.
  In many cases it is a bird or flying insect that has been
  captured and in the past I have had many examples of these types
  sent in.
  However, there are some examples such as the photo taken by
  Roland Rozario, a traffic engineer, in Melbourne Australia who
  took a dozen or so photos and on one of them was a very clear
  UFO. See:
  www.uforth.com/oz.htm
  for full size image
  As I have mentioned in previous posts there is an anomaly as to
  why this should be.
  My best guess would be that it is a camera's ability to
  fractionalise a second that enables a UFO image to be captured.
  And, if so, there may be an element of camouflage employed by a
  UFO, so that we would be unaware of their presence. But it would
  not fool a camera.

  Regards,
  Joe Faccenda

  Listers:
  The debunking of abductions (using the movie trailer The Fourth
  Kind) has already begun and the movie isn't due out for another
  two weeks!
  Here's a quote from the WSJ Article:
  The Fourth Kind Uses UFO Tales To Build Movie Hype - Trailer
  Wall Street Journal
  http://tinyurl.com/yzh5ckf
  'The movie revolves around a series of real-life disappearances
  that took place in Nome, Alaska -- caused, as the film suggests,
  by aliens. But as local newspapers have pointed out, the FBI
  ruled the disappearances were due to excessive alcohol
  consumption and the harsh winters.'
  Oh - really? Only the 'wingnuts' could come up with this one.
  Who knew that alcohol and cold weather could make a person
  disappear? :)
  I have no idea what this movie is really going to be like - an
  accurate portrayal of abductions or not - but I can say this:
  since my site was listed on The Fourth Kind movie's site less
  than two weeks ago, I've received well over 250,000 hits more
  than I normally would at this time of the month, and my site
  crashed two days ago because of it.

  From: A. J. Gevaerd - Revista UFO <aj.nul>
  Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2009 11:15:29 -0200

  Subject: Brazilian Military Confirm UFOs "Solid" &

  Brazilian Military Document Confirms UFOs "Solid" And Under
  "Intelligent Control"
  Dear Listers:
  As I have informed before, the Brazilian Government declassified
  a few weeks ago a new set of previously secret UFO documents,
  covering the 80s. I also informed you that we already had
  disclosures covering the 50s, 60s and 70s. They have been doing
  the releases by decade. So far over 4,000 pages and 300 photos
  have been disclosed. This time declassification, the 80s, is
  composed of some 800 pages and is very powerful.
  Among the documents released are the reports of UFOs on May 19,
  1986, considered the 'Official UFO Night in Brazil', when 21
  spherical objects, estimated 100 meters in diameter - according
  to military sources - literally jammed air traffic over the
  major Braziian Airports, when several Mirage and F5 jets were
  scrambled to pursue them for ours.
  As most of you already know, at that time the Air Force Minister
  Octavio Moreira Lima went public on national TV networks about
  it the other morning. The pilots and their commanders also spoke
  freely about the pursuits, which occurred over several hours.
  This was a major thing in Brazil.
  Now, when on TV to the whole Nation, the Moreira Lima promised
  that a full report would be issued about the events, considering
  the air-air and air-land radar detections and the pilot
  pursuing, and it would be available in 30 days. And as most of
  the things that happen in my country, when governmental promises
  are involved, this much anticipated document was not released
  then.
  Now we know why!
  Among the important files just released in the 80s package,
  there it is a certain 'Occurrence Report', dated June 02, 1986,
  just a few days after the 'invasion' by 21 UFOs of the most
  developed areas in the country. It is 8 pages and signed by Air
  Brigadier Jose Pessoa Cavalcanti de Albuquerque, acting
  commander of the Brazilian Air Command of Air Defense (COMDA).
  Now, what this report contains is very interesting, and I quote
  its Final Considerations part:
  1. Based on the analysis of above-reported events, it is this
  Command's opinion that, according to the information from the
  controllers, pilots and previously elaborated reports from I
  Cindacta (Air Traffic Control and Aerial Defense Center), that
  there are some points of coincidence regarding radar echoes,
  accelerations, illumination, velocities and behavior, either by
  technical detection or by visual contact.
  2. Some of those coinciding points that we can name are those
  phenomena which exhibited certain constant characteristics, as
  follows:
  a. Produced radar echoes, not only on the Air Defense System,
  but also on the intercepting airplanes simultaneously, with

  b. Change in velocity, from subsonic to supersonic, besides
  hovering capability.
  c. Varied altitude, from below FL-050 to altitudes above FL-400.
  d. Occasionally seen as white, green and yellow lights, and
  sometimes no luminous indication.
  e. Sudden acceleration and deceleration
  And there is more. In the Item 3 of the Final Considerations
  part, the Occurrence Report says clearly that 'the phenomenon
  (UFOs) is solid and reflects intelligence'. See it in full:
  3. As a conclusion of the observed constant facts in almost all
  presentations, it is the opinion of this Command that the
  phenomenon is solid and reflects intelligence by its capacity to
  follow and sustain distance from the observers, as well as to
  fly in formation, and are not necessarily manned craft.

  FOTOCAT Blog October 2009 Update
  Dear List members:
  The FOTOCAT Project's has just been updated and it is available
  at:
  http://fotocat.blogspot.com/
  With a current database comprising 9,650 cases, the blog
  contains the following topics, among others:
  * Links to 3 new pdf publications by the author
  * Footage (3 videos) displayed for 2 cases finally solved, and a
  number of -not previously known- military documents
  * News: FOTOCAT archives receive a copy of the Michel Monnerie files
  * Statistics of 2,000 photographic reports for the 1990 decade
  * Data acquisition status for ball lightning project
  * Information on new books and publications that we recommend

  Good reading!

  Sean, but this is a concept and does not fly-see Wiki below.
  NASA had a flying R/C model[about 17 foot wingspan] of a blended
  wing design using small regular jets but has dropped the design.
  See Wikipedia for full:
  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_X-48
  Excerpt: X-48
  Boeing X-48B flight test vehicle on display at the 2006 Edwards
  Airshow.
  "The Boeing Phantom Works is developing the blended wing body
  aircraft concept in cooperation with the NASA Langley Research
  Center. In a continuing effort to study the flight
  characteristics of the BWB design, a small remote-controlled
  model has been successfully flown. The next step was to fly the
  X-48A in 2004, which was to be built at NASA Langley, but that
  program was later canceled.
  Boeing Phantom Works is focusing current research on a pair of
  models, called the X-48B, which were built under contract by
  Cranfield Aerospace in the United Kingdom. Norman Princen,
  Boeing's chief engineer for the project, said, "Earlier wind-
  tunnel testing and the upcoming flight testing are focused on
  learning more about the BWB's low-speed flight-control
  characteristics, especially during takeoffs and landings.
  Knowing how accurately our models predict these characteristics
  is an important step in the further development of this


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m24-010.shtml[11/12/2011 23:11:55]
Re: The Dudley's Merry Hill UFO Video

  concept."
  A couple of people have made noises about the X-48A being a
  culprit but there is no compelling evidence to support this
  principally because it has only flown as a model at places like
  Edwards and in any case would not be test flown in a public
  area. It would be just plain stupid to do so, not to mention
  illegal. The page you supplied from the BBC is playing a little
  loose with the "silent" facts.
  What is hoped is to make the aircraft smaller utilizing the wing
  as as passenger space thus using less power-hence less fuel.
  Less power plus an overwing hi-pass fanjet will make the
  airplane quieter duing take-off. Once it gets to cruising
  altitude it will be pretty much unheard but conventional jets
  are anyway at 30-45,000 feet.
  This is a far cry from some object hovering noiselssly a few
  hundred feet above the ground.
  >If a "concept" as this has made the public forum, it is usually
  >in practice, already "out there" somewhere.
  That's not true. And these full blown concepts are for airliner
  designs not military [maybe tankers or transports] and they will
  never be silent with jets, but they will be quieter using the
  over-wing masking as does the B2-B bomber and the F-117A. The F-
  22 has a sort of blended wing but it is still noisey.
  Note that the X-48B was on display at the Edwards airshow. Way to
  hide the technology, huh?
  Look for these blended designs to begin showing up in about 20
  years. They are not meant to be stealthy but a lot quieter for
  those people who move near airports for the work and then
  complain about the noise.
  The A-380 and the Boeing "dreamship"-if it ever gets off the
  ground-will use up most of the money being spent on large
  airliners for the next/gen airliner. The Chineses are struggling
  to get their own airliner's built and so are the Russians. These
  are knock-offs of the Boeing 767 and Airbus A-340 designs.
  Don Ledger

  From: William Treurniet <wtreurniet.nul>
  Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2009 12:49:16 -0400
  Archived: Sat, 24 Oct 2009 15:11:23 -0400
  Subject: Re: Abduction Debunking Has Already Begun

  >From: Jason Gammon <BoyintheMachine.nul>
  >To: post.nul
  >Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2009 10:43:14 -0400

  >>From: Kathy Kasten <catraja.nul>
  >>To: post to ufoupdates <post.nul>
  >>Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2009 15:37:26 +0000
  >>Subject: Re: Abduction Debunking Has Already Begun
  >>In my estimation, the entire phenomena that humans refer to as
  >>ufology has to do with humans relationship with their
  >>subconscious.
  >>I am very interested in finding out who and what company wrote
  >>and produced this movie.
  >I wasn't aware the subconscious could appear on radar.
  In the last little while, I've been trying to pass people's ufo-
  related experiences through a filter holding that ufos are joint
  creations of the observers' consciousness and a greater
  consciousness responsible for maintaining the integrity of our
  physical reality. The observed objects are real in the normal
  sense of the word, but they depend for their existence on
  unusual behavior of both kinds of consciousness.
  The relatively simple lights in the sky and their associated
  inexplicable movements might be handled by such a model. Some
  people even report that these objects appear on command and
  respond to their wishes, and this behavior fits quite nicely.
  Perhaps the abduction experiences, which are focused mainly
  around individuals, can also be thought of as joint creations of
  consciousness.
  It's a little harder to understand close encounters of craft and
  occupants in this way, but then again, the only difference may
  be that more of the observers' senses are involved. In the
  Rendlesham Forest case, for example, the object was viewed up
  close by several people and even touched. So the object appeared
  to be part of consensus reality not so different from normal
  experience.
  When the created objects are physically real, they would be
  expected to reflect radar.
  We usually try to explain these experiences in terms of our
  current understanding that reality exists independent of
  consciousness. Perhaps we should turn things around and consider
  how consciousness could be the basis of an every-day reality
  that includes ufos.

  William

  <snip>
  >We usually try to explain these experiences in terms of our
  >current understanding that reality exists independent of
  >consciousness. Perhaps we should turn things around and consider
  >how consciousness could be the basis of an every-day reality
  >that includes UFOs.
  Don't you think the greater consciousness wants to say, cure
  cancer and other diseases, stop hunger, cease all wars, etc.?
  Many that see UFOs, as well as abductees, do _not_ want to
  experience these events on any level for core human value
  reasons. Reasons like personal safety, fear of ridicule, fear of
  the unknown, etc. This goes against what the mind wants. And if
  the consciousness is creating things that the mind doesn't want,
  wouldn't our lives be filled with all kinds of inexplicable
  terror?
  I think there is much more theoretical evidence for alternate
  dimensions or planes of existence then our minds creating
  physical reality. And it would be easier to believe that
  thoughts could be read, then our minds not only creating but
  collaborating on making the same type of reality. But I don't
  think we will know the truth in our lifetimes or maybe even in
  this millennia.

  Bill

A Big Breakthrough In Ufology?




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2009 > Oct > Oct 26

                                                   A Big Breakthrough In Ufology?
  From: Nick Balaskas <nikolaos.nul>
  Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2009 23:11:46 -0400
  Archived: Mon, 26 Oct 2009 09:10:00 -0400
  Subject: A Big Breakthrough In Ufology?

  Hi Everyone!
  "If some of the frequently reported mysterious and unexplained
  lights seen in the night sky are indeed extraterrestrial craft
  that freely and stealthily fly about in our airspace, why would
  these UFOs have bright running lights that only serve to attract
  attention to their presence?"
  This is a question I frequently hear from skeptical science
  colleagues - something they also use as an excuse to explain
  away all UFO sightings as misidentified aircraft and to avoid
  doing further investigation into this phenomenon.
  With the arrival of a "proof copy" of a new book last Wednesday

Re: Abduction Debunking Has Already Begun


  I proposed that these phenomena may be a possibly involuntary
  joint project between human consciousness and a larger
  consciousness, for lack of a better word. I suggest, because it
  is a joint project, you would not necessarily be in control of
  the situation. As an analogy, let's say that this larger
  consciousness is like the sun. When you interact with it, your
  skin may burn or not depending on how fair-skinned you are.
  Nothing you can do can alter the outcome, short of moving into
  the shade. You may abhor the sun as the pain from the burn
  increases, or you can take the sun for granted as the tan
  deepens. Consistent with this analogy, what abductees experience
  may depend on the properties of their own consciousness. Some
  find the experience oppressive while others seem to find it
  enlightening.
  I propose that experiencers may be interacting with a force of
  nature that is also conscious. In my paper, referenced earlier,
  I called it the universal observer. I proposed that its
  parameters determine the laws of nature and the continuous
  creation of form and function in the material world. Because we
  are conscious, we should also, in principle, be able to modify
  the rules imposed by the universal observer and change physical
  reality. Most of us non-experiencers can't or won't do this. The
  experiencers, however, somehow find themselves involuntarily
  fiddling with the structure of reality. Because it is
  involuntary, the ego seems not to be involved, so we cannot
  adjust reality just to win lotteries.
  Of course, this theory would not apply to human interventions
  such as military abductions, if they occur. I understand this is
  still unresolved. On the other hand, there are stories about
  human crop circle makers experiencing paranormal effects in
  their formations. Perhaps their actions helped their
  consciousness twiddle the knobs controlling reality's
  parameters. Similarly, milab abductions, although initiated by
  humans, might also cross the line into the paranormal.

  Best,
  William

  into a fictional invasion-from-space flick. He fought hard,
  albeit unsuccessfully, to have his name removed from the
  credits. I don't know what he was thinking -- maybe about UFOs'
  respectability out of all proportion -- but there is nothing
  disgraceful about being connected with this thoroughly
  entertaining movie.

   Dear Listers,

   I am pleased to announce that with the efforts of 'The Few', the

   www.the ufoguy.org has been suspended by its host Bravenet.
   It's important to point out, that this is the _third_ site that
   has been shut down in under two years; Knell sees this as "the
   cost of doing business!" He has been doing this for decades, and
   simply having his site closed does not stifle him overall. He
   does have other 'scam-sites', not related to Ufology, and his
   Amazon site is still up.
   In short, as surely as the sun will rise tomorrow, Knell will
   continue his nefarious ways, that is until he is arrested and
   punished to the fullest extent of the law. Henceforth, this is
   why any potential victims "follow through with their respective
   complaints."
   The names of the potential victims, as listed below were culled
   in haste, and taken from DVDs that Knell had offered for sale on
   his web-site; separately, through the efforts of myself and
   complainant Scott Ramsey et al, we've confirmed over 30 victims!
   These people were contacted directly and in most cases, verified
   that Knell was not authorized in any form or fashion to sell
   their copyrighted work!
   Because many of the examples of copyright infringement were
   lectures from various symposia, "authorized" distributors were
   contacted, as well as symposium promoters who often times retain
   the right to market the various lectures of their speakers etc.;
   it was no surprise to find out that these folks were not only
   cognizant of Knell's criminal activities, but that they had
   taken actions against him in various degrees in the past. They,
   as well as the original copyright owners "never" authorized
   Knell to sell and or reproduce the respective works.
   Out of every suspected victim contacted, ALL were being ripped
   off!! There was no "hit and miss"--it was 100%! In that vein, I
   believe that out of the names listed below, the majority (if not
   all) where copyright is still in force are having their legal
   rights violated. (Remember too, that there are many more names
   not listed).
   Most potential victims are not aware of the crimes against them;
   the purpose of the original notice was/is to inform folks that
   their rights were being violated and they can help put an end to
   it; that they are not alone and collectively they can put Knell
   out of business once and for all.
   Although the thesis of my missives have been focused on the
   copyright holders, it's essential to underscore the
   _other_victims_ who far out number the authors of said works,
   i.e., the buyers of bogus, poorly pirated, illegal DVDs! Given
   the longevity of Knell's criminal enterprises, as well as the

                                                              The Blimp Is Back
  From: Joe McGonagle <joe.mcgonagle.nul>

  Subject: The Blimp Is Back

  Soure: Soldier Magazine
  http://www.soldiermagazine.co.uk/mag/feature1.htm
  The Blimp Is Back
  by Andrew Simms
  There is no denying that the stock of the blimp has deflated
  dramatically since the glory age of the airship in the early
  1900s.
  Once heralded as the transportation of the future and
  anticipated to become so popular that the art deco spire of New
  York=92s Empire State Building was originally intended as a
  mooring point, the airship has more recently been relegated to
  hovering over sporting events and advertising Goodyear tyres.
  However, with the help of British expertise and at the request
  of the US Army, plans are under way to relaunch the military
  career of the blimp.
  Having served as an aerial scout and primitive bomber with
  British, American and German forces during the two world wars,
  the airship is once again in vogue.
  And lighter-than-air technology has already played its part in
  the international effort to defeat the Taliban through a state-
  of-the-art observation balloon boasting advanced surveillance
  capabilities, which is deployed several thousand feet above the
  Afghan capital of Kabul. Anchored at Bala Hissar, the aerostat
  gave coalition commanders a bird=92s eye view of the city -- and
  more importantly the movements of insurgents -- during August=92s
  election.
  But the blue-sky thinking of the major defence contractors goes
  far beyond tethered balloons. Raytheon recently unveiled its
  first Joint Land Attack Cruise Missile Defense Elevated Netted
  Sensor System (JLENS) -- one of 12 helium-filled blimps being
  developed to provide cover for US ground forces. Equipped with
  radars capable of detecting threats up to 300 miles away, JLENS
  will be able to stay in flight for 30 days at a time and has
  been designed to track enemy missiles.
  In turn, Lockheed Martin is building a prototype of a radar-
  equipped airship. Scheduled to take its maiden flight in 2012,
  this solar/fuel cell-powered system will operate at altitudes of
  60,000ft and be able to track cruise missiles at 600km and
  dismounted soldiers at 300km. It is estimated that such a near-
  space asset will be capable of surveying millions of cubic miles
  of airspace.
  The company is also exploring the production of a Hybrid
  Unmanned Air Vehicle (HUAV). Envisaged as a means of moving
  equipment -- and even troops -- in low-threat military
  environments, it is anticipated that the HUAV will be able to
  lift loads of up to 12,000lbs at 10,000ft.
  Timothy Blunck, a flight test engineer for Lockheed Martin, told
  Soldier that talk of a return to airships was more than just hot


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m27-013.shtml[11/12/2011 23:12:18]
The Blimp Is Back

  air.
  =93Is this old technology? Yes it is, but it is proven technology
  which, when combined with advancements in other fields, you can
  do a lot of mind-blowing stuff with,=94 he said. =93What lighter-
  than-air technology gives you is a far greater degree of
  persistence and economical vehicles which can save on manpower.
  =93You can launch an airship once and forget about it, unlike
  smaller UAVs which you have to pull back a day or two later.
  With these platforms you can lift the scale and perform theatre-
  wide missions.=94
  A series of high-profile accidents, such as the burning of the
  Hindenburg, sped the decline of airships last time round, but
  Blunck insisted the use of helium rather than hydrogen and
  advancements in durability means that the blimp bubble is
  unlikely to burst soon.
  =93There is a slight assumption of air supremacy, but for the US
  and UK that is not usually a problem,=94 he added. =93That said, at
  60,000ft there is not a great deal of traffic or weaponry about.
  Even the HUAV, which would be flying at 20,000ft in a tactical
  scenario, would be beyond the reach of most mobile weapons.=94
  Operating out of harm=92s way, blimps could soon be deployed in a
  host of roles not viable for fixed-wing aircraft -- taking to the
  battlefield as either a communications relay, spy satellite,
  missile defence system, floating refuelling station or even a
  portable airstrip.
  And so, while the exact flight path may not yet be known, after
  more than seven decades in the hangar it seems that the sky is
  once again the limit for the airship.

   About UFOs
   Brazil=92s former Air Force minister Socrates Monteiro was

   Last Sunday, October 25th, Brazilian UFO Magazine interviewed

   Fernando Collor, from 1990-1992, lieutenant-brigadier Socrates
   da Costa Monteiro. The interview was conducted in his residence
   in Rio de Janeiro and was performed by this editor A. J.
   Gevaerd, with the cooperation of the co-editor Marco Antonio
   Petit and the consultants Francisco Pires de Campos and Arthur
   Ferreira Neto. It was more than two hours of extremely
   interesting and fruitful conversation, in which the military
   felt comfortable to talk about Ufology, like some other
   officials who also gave their statements to Brazilian UFO
   Magazine.
   Monteiro is retired from the Brazilian Air Force (FAB) for a
   number of years, but keeps his bounds with active militaries
   from various sectors of the Brazilian military. He has an
   extremely lucid memory of the major facts of his activities in
   the Air Force and =96 of special interest to the Ufology =96 about
   how the country handled with the matter during the time when he
   was on active duty. Like other ministers, before and after him,
   Monteiro also had access to sensitive information on the
   interaction of other cosmic species in our country, reporting a
   few cases. He was pilot of many airplane types, including
   fighters, gathering more than 5 thousand flight hours in them.
   =93Technology far more advanced than ours=94

   Air Traffic Control Centre (Cindacta), in <?xml:namespace prefix
   =3D st1 ns =3D "urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:smarttags"

   assumed its command, and that all the cases were carefully
   registered, with some of them being further investigated by the
   Air Force. In that occasion the expression =93Traffic Hotel=94 was
   not yet used to designate UFOs.
   Monteiro described a situation when the radar station of
   Cindacta in Gama (DF) was overflown at low altitude by a disk
   type object of great proportions, and that its staff, without
   knowing what to do, opened fire against the =93intruder=94. When he

  Hi Dave,
  The short answer to your question is "yes" - except that these
  lights are not just the effect of some "futuristic" propulsion
  system but one that exists and is available to us now.
  A few years ago the author demonstrated a working model based on
  this futuristic propulsion system to me. The changes in the
  brightness and range of colours reported for UFOs when they take
  off or land and while in flight, especially when they rapidly
  accelerate or make sudden changes in direction, is reproduced by
  Stoyan's propulsion system.
  Also, the unique flight characteristics of UFOs as well as other
  reported effects such as optical distortions around the UFO and
  the audible sounds recorded (such as the recordings made by my
  friend Chris Purton, another York University space scientist,
  who personally investigated local ongoing UFO sightings) also
  can be accounted for by Stoyan's propulsion system.

  up another point..
  Why do people in the UFO field accept every hypothesis and
  postulation as being equally valid? They are definitely not.
  The ETH, although unproven to date, is our best bet as it is
  rooted in reality.
  For me at least, the ETH, "outside earth", encompasses beings
  from other planets, beings from parallel universes, and even
  time travelers. They aren't form here, therefore they can be
  included in the ETH. However, certain critics of the ETH don't
  see it that way at all. They want to postulate fanciful and
  absurd hypotheses and postulations that are not rooted in
  reality and which have absolutely no chance of ever being
  proven. To make matters worse, many of such proponents then
  turn around and act like their fantastical concepts are now
  proven or have somehow "trumped" the ETH.
  Honestly, many people do not understand how to think
  Scientifically. Such people blur religion, spirituality,
  fantasy, and pseudoscience into a wicked pot of goulash they
  then attempt to force feed others. Well, I for one will not eat
  it.
  If it's not Science, then it's worthless. Religion,
  Spirituality, and Magic cannot be distinguished from Fantasy and
  Delusion.

  >useful, here, either. I suspect that that's not science, too.

  Universe, even if for only brief periods of time, say through
  time travel or travel from a parallel universe.
  It would be an error to claim UFOs represent something we can't
  understand or are not able to identify.
  Juvenile certainty? Wow, you must have left Science a long time
  ago.
  Science is not a democracy. Science doesn't cater to personal
  feelings or beliefs. Science shows no favor to superstition.
  Science is extremely conservative because it has to be.
  The goal, Alfred, is to get mainstream Science to embrace the
  UFO mystery. As long as we have people pushing for non-
  scientific explanations that have no basis in reality then such
  goal will never be met.

  abductions,a landing at a desert launch facility that starts off
  like the legendary Holloman encounter, telepathy and mind
  control, the development of anti-saucer raygun technology, even

  this was one way these memes were first planted in our group
  consciousness.

                                                                Are You Ready?
  From: Greg Boone <Evolbaby.nul>
  Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2009 06:08:44 EDT
  Archived: Wed, 28 Oct 2009 12:15:00 -0400
  Subject: Are You Ready?

  With the new alien abduction movie, Fourth Kind and the hit song
  by The Killers all dealing with the subject, are you ready to
  field the questions and handle the potential surge of public
  inquiries into the subject?
  I'm surprised at how there are so many people, mostly people
  I've know my entire life who are now coming forward with their
  abduction stories. Folks I never would have guessed have finally
  felt comfortable enough to discuss it in the open.
  What they've told me of their experiences is just mind boggling
  at how they could go on their day to day activities. If it
  doesn't drive them mad.
  I'm learning that in the old days they had turned to alcohol and
  dope to ease the situation but would never have come forward for
  fear of psychiatric incarceration. When I was growing up back
  east if you said you'd been abducted the authorities would have
  rushed you to the nearest headshrinker and you would not come
  out with your sanity. There were many people in the area most
  folks knew of who'd been abducted or claimed to have been who
  were totally normal until they got the padded room, electro
  shock treatment.
  With the publicity these new entertainment venues are getting
  that aren't dealing with big sci-fi UFO invasions but with the
  most terrifying aspect of the phenom, it would be wise to have
  your notes ready.
  Unfortunately I couldn't send anyone to hypnotists for the
  regression stuff. I'm personally against it. Each of us has our
  own methods but if this stuff ramps up to the point the
  floodgates are opened regarding the abduction phenomenon then
  it's a sure bet that some official source is going to have to
  address it.
  Let's hope it ain't the psychiatrists or they'll appoint it as a
  new one of their diseases and try to get the victims forced onto
  some toxic mind altering pharmaceuticals.
  The ride may be about to start folks. Choose your seats and
  sides.

  Best,
  Greg

http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2009/oct/m28-016.shtml[11/12/2011 23:13:44]
It's Just Not Science

   >>our normal understanding of "real", then the subject is not
   >>worth researching or discussing.
   >>To conclude that UFOs are Subconscious Projections, or even the
   >>work of fairies or witches is to accept a claim without any
   >>proof or evidence. Strike that, it's actually worse as it
   >>includes the ignoring of the physical data implying the
   >>phenomena is grounded in reality, such as radar confirmations.
   >>I don't care who the person is, be they a big name in the field
   >>or not. If one is pushing for a magical explanation for the UFO
   >>phenomena then we should treat such people as "biblical lepers".
   >>Such individuals have wandered off the path of Science and are
   >>hopelessly lost in fantasy land.
   >>-Jason
   >This type of theory has been floating around whenever anything
   >new comes into our existence and threatens the status quo.
   >Delusions don't leave trace cases and don't show up on radar.
   >If they do then we need to rethink our own reality and our
   >participation in it.
   Greg
   Apparently mathematicians in the name of something called
   "conscious realism" are doing just what you suggest and
   rethinking our reality.
   I am informed by friends who better understand these things
   that:
   Conscious realism requires that we adopt the notion that
   consciousness- rather than matter - is fundamental. It
   acknowledges an objective reality but quickly cautions that
   conscious beings (such as humans) do not have direct access to
   objective reality.
   Instead, we have access to a symbolic iconography which we
   believe to be reality.
   Since we don't have direct access to objective reality,
   everything we know is based on our subjective experience: our
   observations of that iconographic symbolism. This of course
   includes our sciences and "physical laws". So we are constrained
   by our observational abilities. Anomalous phenomena, far from
   something to dismiss, is in reality an indicator that our
   synthesis of reliable observations, what some like to call
   'science', is incomplete. Instead of refuting such anomalies, it
   is the job of science to explain them.
   Furthermore conscious realism states that this perceptual
   iconography is created by networks of conscious agents, some of
   whom, like humans, are likely hierarchical in nature. It is the
   consensus of these conscious agents which creates the
   iconography we all recognize. And while all humans are conscious
   agents, conscious realists suggest that not all conscious agents
   are human. Indeed some may be of forms either never or rarely
   encountered by humans directly. This opens the interesting door
   for experiences with the deceased, aliens and various other
   interesting things.
   Search for "Observer Mechanics" and "Conscious Realism" on the
   Web.
   One direct link to papers written by the original authors of the
   mathematical theory is:
   http://www.cogsci.uci.edu/~ddhoff/ompref.html
   at Univ. of California, Irvine.
   A more readable paper on Conscious Realism:
   http://www.cogsci.uci.edu/~ddhoff/ConsciousRealism2.pdf
   also at UCI.

  Reinventing the wheel indeed, Don
  My dear late friend Len Cramp invented a prototype for a closely
  related craft back in the 1970s. Len's version was effectively a
  hybrid blimp/hovercraft which used LTA and rocket boost
  technology to create a fuel efficient hovercraft that could
  handle difficult terrain by cutting in the rocket boost to
  traverse obstacles or uneven ground that normal hovercraft would
  find impassable.
  With current computer technology to automate sensors and the
  boost effect Len's invention would be far more viable today than
  when he first came up with the idea.
  As ever with Len, his work on this was driven by humanitarian
  principles: he had been distressed by the fact that conventional
  hovercraft were unable to fulfil the vision of bringing a cost-
  effective transport solution to a plethora of third-world
  situations where geographical isolation had been identified as
  the most significant barrier to economic progress. Even now his
  invention could make a big difference, but its lack of military
  potential will no doubt keep it firmly on the drawing board.
  And before the technically illiterate start to suggest that
  Len's invention may have been implemented as a secret project

                                        Re: Abduction Debunking Has Already Begun
  From: Michael Tarbell <mtarbell.nul>
  Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2009 13:53:08 -0700
  Archived: Thu, 29 Oct 2009 07:55:15 -0400
  Subject: Re: Abduction Debunking Has Already Begun

  >From: Jason Gammon <boyinthemachine.nul>
  >To: post.nul
  >Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2009 12:33:52 -0400
  >Subject: Re: Abduction Debunking Has Already Begun
  <snip>
  >Why do people in the UFO field accept every hypothesis and
  >postulation as being equally valid? They are definitely not.
  >The ETH, although unproven to date, is our best bet as it is
  >rooted in reality.
  >For me at least, the ETH, "outside earth", encompasses beings
  >from other planets, beings from parallel universes, and even
  >time travelers. They aren't form here, therefore they can be
  >included in the ETH. However, certain critics of the ETH don't
  >see it that way at all. They want to postulate fanciful and
  >absurd hypotheses and postulations that are not rooted in
  >reality and which have absolutely no chance of ever being
  >proven. To make matters worse, many of such proponents then
  >turn around and act like their fantastical concepts are now
  >proven or have somehow "trumped" the ETH.

  Hi Jason,
  I think you are expressing a frustration felt by at least
  several others on the List. For better or worse, it is a free-
  for-all, and a lot of stuff is going into the stew that, from a
  scientific perspective, doesn't belong there.
  For example, consider the recent suggestions to the effect that
  UFOs are simply projections of our subconcious mind, radar
  returns and all.
  Well, one certainly can't rule out that possibility. Indeed,
  that's the whole problem with the idea... it's utterly non-
  falsifiable. The entirety of the universe could just as well be
  my own mental projection. An intiguing concept I suppose, but
  one for which further discussion is completely pointless.
  A scientific investigation of UFOs should start with the default
  presumption of a physical, objective mechanism, rather than a
  metaphysical, subjective one, until such point that it clearly
  not possible for the former to account for the observations.
  The study of UFOs is nowhere near that point. Compared to, say,
  quantum physics, the spectrum of UFO phenomena is downright
  mundane... even _oddly_ mundane, as has been discussed here
  previously.
  I see no justification at this point for appeal to metaphysical,
  spritual, or mental-projectual theories. Or even the ETH, for
  that matter. Whatever plausibility the latter has derives mainly
  from the fact that we have good reasons, _independent_ of UFO
  phenomena, to suspect that life should be widespread in the
  universe.
